transcript.text: Hi, we've just had a Bosch KGN36VLEAG delivered last week and it makes a gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, plus a click every so often and a crack noise at night. Is it faulty? It's driving my husband mad.

It is unlikely to be faulty from those sounds alone. Gurgling/bubbling is normally refrigerant moving through a new fridge-freezer, and cracking or popping at night is commonly the plastic liner expanding and contracting during cooling or automatic defrost. An occasional click as the compressor starts or stops is also normal. What would make it a fault is repeated click-clicking every few minutes without proper cooling, a loud buzzing with no cooling, or hissing accompanied by oily residue. 1. Check it is standing firm and level, with nothing at the back touching the wall, cupboards or pipework. A slight vibration can make ordinary running noises much more noticeable.
2. Make sure it has the clearance specified in its handbook and is not tightly boxed in. A newly installed appliance can run more often while it settles and reaches temperature.
3. Is it cooling normally, and is the click just occasional with a steady hum afterwards, rather than repeated clicking every few minutes? That separates normal cycling from a compressor-start problem. If it is cooling properly and the noises are intermittent rather than a constant rattle or repeated clicking, this is normal operation rather than a fault. As it was only delivered last week, use the retailer/Bosch warranty route if the noise is exceptionally loud, worsening, or accompanied by poor cooling.

Thank you. It's level, with a gap either side and behind, and nothing is touching it. It's cooling well, showing 4C in the fridge and -18C in the freezer. The click is just one now and then, followed by quiet for ages, and there's a steady low hum while it runs. There's no burning smell and nothing has tripped. Is the gurgling when the motor starts or stops still normal?

Yes. Gurgling or bubbling as the motor/compressor starts or stops is still normal: refrigerant pressure is changing and moving through the cooling circuit. It can sound rather like water running, especially on a newly installed fridge-freezer. The night-time crack is also consistent with the cabinet liner expanding and contracting as it cools or goes through defrost. There is no fault pattern here at present. It would be worth using the retailer or Bosch warranty only if the sound becomes a constant loud rattle/buzz, the appliance stops holding temperature, or it begins repeated click-hum-click attempts every few minutes.

Vibration from installation or something touching the cabinet (low)
